ENC2055 Midterm Exam Performance Report

Overall Score Distribution and Section-by-Section Analysis

November 26, 2026

Overview

This report summarizes student performance on the ENC2055 Midterm Exam (\(N = 14\)). Both the overall grade distribution and section-by-section scores are visualized so students can benchmark their performance against the class distribution across every component of the exam. To protect student privacy, raw student IDs are replaced with randomized anonymous codes in individual-level visualizations.

library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(htmltools)

# Load midterm exam scores (ensure ENC2055_midterm.xlsx is in the same directory as this .Rmd file)
raw_df <- read_excel("ENC2055_midterm.xlsx")

# Create randomized anonymous codes (Student 01–Student 14) so row order does not leak spreadsheet position
set.seed(2055)
anon_df <- raw_df %>%
  slice_sample(prop = 1) %>%
  mutate(
    Anon_ID = sprintf("Student %02d", row_number())
  )

# Tidy section scores into long format using only anonymized identifiers
sections_long <- anon_df %>%
  select(Anon_ID, starts_with("Section")) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("Section"),
    names_to = "Section",
    values_to = "Score"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Section = factor(
      Section,
      levels = c("Section 1", "Section 2", "Section 3", "Section 4", "Section 5")
    )
  )

# Compute summary statistics for total score
total_stats <- anon_df %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Mean = mean(`Total Grade`, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(`Total Grade`, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(`Total Grade`, na.rm = TRUE),
    IQR = IQR(`Total Grade`, na.rm = TRUE),
    Min = min(`Total Grade`, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max = max(`Total Grade`, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

1. Overall Midterm Performance

The horizontal boxplot below displays the overall class distribution of total exam grades. Because the cohort has 14 students, every individual score is overlaid as a jittered point alongside the median (solid vertical line inside the box) and class mean (diamond marker).

set.seed(2055)

ggplot(anon_df, aes(x = `Total Grade`, y = "ENC2055 Cohort")) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.36,
    fill = "#d6eaf8",
    color = "#1f618d",
    alpha = 0.85,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    height = 0.09,
    width = 0,
    size = 3.2,
    color = "#1a5276",
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    shape = 18,
    size = 4.5,
    color = "#c0392b"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = total_stats$Mean,
    y = 1.28,
    label = sprintf("Mean: %.2f", total_stats$Mean),
    color = "#c0392b",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.8
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = total_stats$Median,
    y = 0.72,
    label = sprintf("Median: %.1f", total_stats$Median),
    color = "#1f618d",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.8
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(50, 95, by = 5), limits = c(52, 90)) +
  labs(
    title = "Overall Midterm Exam Score Distribution",
    subtitle = "Box shows interquartile range (25th–75th percentile); dots represent individual students (N = 14)",
    x = "Total Grade",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, color = "#1a252f"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10.5, color = "#566573", margin = margin(b = 12)),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#2c3e50")
  )

2. Section-by-Section Performance

Exam sections carry different maximum point values (observed highs reach 27 points in Section 1, 20 points in Sections 4 and 5, 12 points in Section 2, and 9 points in Section 3). To make comparisons clear across sections, the visualizations below present both raw score distributions and normalized percentage attainment (each student’s score divided by the highest observed score in that section).

2.1 Raw Score Distributions Across Sections

Grouped boxplots with overlaid student points show the spread, median, and clustering of raw scores within each exam section.

set.seed(2055)

section_palette <- c(
  "Section 1" = "#2874a6",
  "Section 2" = "#148f77",
  "Section 3" = "#d68910",
  "Section 4" = "#7d3c98",
  "Section 5" = "#cb4335"
)

ggplot(sections_long, aes(x = Section, y = Score, fill = Section, color = Section)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.48,
    alpha = 0.25,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.12,
    height = 0,
    size = 2.8,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    shape = 18,
    size = 3.8,
    color = "#1a252f"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = section_palette) +
  scale_color_manual(values = section_palette) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 30, by = 3)) +
  labs(
    title = "Score Distribution by Exam Section (Raw Points)",
    subtitle = "Colored boxes show IQR and median; black diamonds mark section means; dots show individual scores",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Raw Score"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, color = "#1a252f"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10.5, color = "#566573", margin = margin(b = 12)),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11.5)
  )

2.2 Relative Mastery by Section (Normalized Cleveland Dot & Mean Plot)

Because raw point scales differ across sections, normalizing scores relative to the observed section maximum (Score / Max Observed Score) highlights where the class performed strongest and where students encountered the greatest difficulty.

# NOTE: Update `Max_Observed` below if an official rubric max differs from the observed class max.
section_summary <- sections_long %>%
  group_by(Section) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(Score),
    SD = sd(Score),
    Median = median(Score),
    IQR = IQR(Score),
    Min = min(Score),
    Max_Observed = max(Score),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Mean_Pct = (Mean / Max_Observed) * 100,
    Median_Pct = (Median / Max_Observed) * 100
  )

ggplot(section_summary, aes(y = fct_rev(Section))) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = 0, xend = Mean_Pct, yend = fct_rev(Section), color = Section),
    linewidth = 2.2,
    alpha = 0.75
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(x = Mean_Pct, color = Section),
    size = 5
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      x = Mean_Pct,
      label = sprintf("%.1f%% (Mean: %.2f / %d)", Mean_Pct, Mean, Max_Observed)
    ),
    hjust = -0.1,
    size = 3.8,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#2c3e50"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = section_palette) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 122),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 20),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Attainment by Section (% of Observed Section Maximum)",
    subtitle = "Enables fair comparison of relative difficulty across sections with different point weights",
    x = "Mean Attainment (%)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, color = "#1a252f"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10.5, color = "#566573", margin = margin(b = 12)),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11.5)
  )

2.3 Individual Student Performance Profile (Anonymized Heatmap)

To preserve privacy, original student IDs are omitted and replaced with randomly assigned codes (Student 01–Student 14). Students can locate their own row by matching their exact section and total score combination (ordered from highest to lowest total grade).

heatmap_df <- sections_long %>%
  left_join(
    anon_df %>% select(Anon_ID, `Total Grade`),
    by = "Anon_ID"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Section) %>%
  mutate(Pct_of_Max = Score / max(Score)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    Student_Label = sprintf("%s  (Total: %d)", Anon_ID, `Total Grade`),
    Student_Label = fct_reorder(Student_Label, `Total Grade`)
  )

ggplot(heatmap_df, aes(x = Section, y = Student_Label, fill = Pct_of_Max)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = Score,
      color = ifelse(Pct_of_Max > 0.62, "white", "#1a252f")
    ),
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_color_identity() +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = c("#f9ebea", "#f5b7b1", "#5dade2", "#2874a6", "#1b4f72"),
    limits = c(0, 1),
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    name = "Relative
Score"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Anonymized Student-by-Section Score Matrix",
    subtitle = "Randomized labels (Student 01–14) ordered by Total Grade; cell numbers show raw section scores",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12.5) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, color = "#1a252f"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10.5, color = "#566573", margin = margin(b = 12)),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11.5),
    axis.text.y = element_text(family = "mono", size = 10.5)
  )

3. Summary Statistics Table

summary_table <- section_summary %>%
  transmute(
    Component = as.character(Section),
    Mean = sprintf("%.2f", Mean),
    SD = sprintf("%.2f", SD),
    Median = sprintf("%.1f", Median),
    IQR = sprintf("%.2f", IQR),
    Range = sprintf("%d – %d", Min, Max_Observed),
    `Mean % of Max` = sprintf("%.1f%%", Mean_Pct)
  ) %>%
  bind_rows(
    tibble(
      Component = "Total Grade",
      Mean = sprintf("%.2f", total_stats$Mean),
      SD = sprintf("%.2f", total_stats$SD),
      Median = sprintf("%.1f", total_stats$Median),
      IQR = sprintf("%.2f", total_stats$IQR),
      Range = sprintf("%d – %d", total_stats$Min, total_stats$Max),
      `Mean % of Max` = "—"
    )
  )

kable(
  summary_table,
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "c", "r"),
  caption = "Descriptive Statistics for ENC2055 Midterm Exam (N = 14)"
)
